summary.prose: This story defines and validates the records and release manifests used by the design corpus. It makes required guidance and provenance explicit, gives unchanged content reproducible identifiers, and preserves all inspectable metadata through serialization. It provides validation contracts and fixtures for later ingestion, curation and retrieval stories.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose immutable release packages with a daemon-owned catalog and rebuildable retrieval indexes. Shared contracts below are proposed additions, not existing APIs. Corpus data is global public knowledge, independent of registered source repositories; DI2 owns project-private guideline storage and DI3 owns authoring workflows.

ownedContracts.name: Corpus record and pinned evidence identity
ownedContracts.purpose: Common immutable record, provenance and release identity across all stories and DI2/DI3.

ownedContracts.name: Release manifest and publication gate
ownedContracts.purpose: s1 establishes envelopes and gates used by import, curation, query and maintenance; s2 implements ingestion. Publication requires nonempty problem/tradeoffs, checks with explicit limits (or an explicit no-measurable-check rationale), and domainPayload.color/layout/style for corresponding color/layout/style records. Semantic roles and pairings must reference declared roles; examples and misuse examples must be present for every declared platform. Domain validation rejects an empty placeholder.

boundary.internal: Own canonical schema, version/hash specification, publication validation interfaces and fixtures. This is the nearest ancestor for all shared identity/release contracts; storage and curator UI are not implied.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own source adapters, local staging extraction, allowlist policy implementation and reproducible notices. Adapter specifics stay private; no unreviewed source contents enter published assets.

Own authored seed records, declarative specimens and reviewed coverage across ten domains and three UI types. A release names its maintainer/reviewer; unknown source sufficiency cannot be counted as coverage.

Own daemon package reader, catalog read adapter, deterministic filtering/ranking, local embedding cache, cursor implementation and thin MCP read tools. Keep ranking weights and cache format private and versioned. Basic validated bundled-package installation is included so retrieval is independently testable. Includes the single-sourced config-catalog entry, typed config exposure, settings/reconciliation verification and catalog contract-test update. Owns vscode-plugin/package.json setting mirror and verification of the unchanged catalog-driven JetBrains SettingsView.kt, validated by manifest/catalog parity and settings render/round-trip checks. Sole owner of catalog file layout, serialized atomic commit, receipts and recovery via sc7. Basic installation and maintenance use exactly this writer.

Own update staging, atomic publish/default switch, withdrawal overlays, recovery, release diffs and cross-release regression evaluation. Consume existing reader contracts; never change DI2 guideline state. Uses sc7 for all catalog/default/availability changes; owns upstream update policy and diff orchestration only, not a second writer or recovery implementation.

nonFunctional.performance: For a representative 1,000-record seed fixture, measure warm query p95 <=500 ms excluding local embedding inference; report embedding latency separately. This is a target, not a benchmark claim. If exceeded, optimize indexing without dropping eligible candidates; complete-result quality takes precedence. Cold index building is resumable and serial.
nonFunctional.security: Only eligible reviewed material is distributed. Validate all package paths and sizes, reject executable specimen content and remote includes; escape rendering. No arbitrary URL fetching at query time. Unknown hard constraints return gaps. Do not mix project-private data into the public corpus or embedding index.
nonFunctional.observability: Log release ID, query mode, eligible/matched counts, filter/gap reasons, index fingerprint and validation codes; avoid storing user query/brief text by default. Expose install/index health and explicit degraded retrieval, rather than silent fallback.
nonFunctional.durability: Immutable package bytes plus atomic catalog and append-only availability events. Rebuild derived indexes on checksum/model mismatch. Inject crashes between each publication boundary; old release remains readable or a newly complete release becomes visible, never partial content. Retain pinned references across rollback; policy withdrawal returns tombstones.

api.name: GuidanceRecord

returns.meaning: Complete decoded JSON record; validation preserves every declared field and never coerces, defaults or strips input.

errors.condition: Wrong schema, missing field, unexpected property, invalid domain data, incomplete provenance, digest mismatch or stale review.

preconditions: Accept unknown decoded JSON at validation boundaries; types alone never establish validity.
Draft records retain the full HLD shape, with empty review reviewer/time/digest allowed only while status is draft.
postconditions: A record admitted for publication has nonblank required guidance, complete sc1 provenance and an exact content-bound reviewed status.
Record serialization/decoding preserves identity, version, relations, rationale, authorship and source references; it does not perform retrieval.

api.name: ReleaseManifest

returns.meaning: Validated manifest referencing a closed, unique package inventory; not an installed or published release.

errors.condition: Duplicate identity/path, missing referenced file, invalid relative path, unresolved exact record relationship, unknown schema or mismatched digest.

preconditions: Caller supplies immutable in-memory file inventory including bytes and file kind; no filesystem, network or DB access in this story.
The manifest is excluded from its own files list; every referenced data file appears exactly once.
postconditions: All manifest record pairs and referenced package files are present; digest calculation follows the approved dependency order.
Validating a manifest does not mutate catalog state, import sources or claim editorial approval.

api.name: PublicationCheck
api.signature: interface PublicationCheck { eligible: boolean; issues: ValidationIssue[]; manifestDigest: string; }

parameters.name: candidate
parameters.purpose: Decoded sc1/sc2 content and bounded immutable package inventory to validate.

parameters.name: assessments
parameters.type: readonly { stage: 'eligibility' | 'coverage'; candidateContentDigest: string; passed: boolean; issues: ValidationIssue[] }[]
parameters.purpose: Digest-bound validation results supplied by downstream adapters. s1 only composes them; it does not implement sc3/sc4 policy.

returns.meaning: Pure preflight decision; manifestDigest is SHA-256 of canonical manifest excluding releaseId when computable, otherwise empty. eligible implies zero issues and successful exact-digest assessments.

errors.condition: All expected validation failures are returned with stable code, JSON Pointer path and message; no thrown domain error.

preconditions: Exactly one assessment per required stage. Missing, duplicate, stale, failed, or contradictory assessment fails closed.
Assessment objects are trusted internal composition results, not user-issued authorization tokens; only downstream daemon orchestration produces them.
postconditions: eligible is true only when record/domain/manifest/hash checks and both supplied stages pass.
No admission, persistent publication or side effects occur; schema compilation faults are programmer/configuration failures, not user validation failures.

dataModelChanges.details: Implement the exact approved sc1 type in proposed src/design/corpus/contracts.ts with TypeBox schemas and Static-derived readonly-facing types. Use closed objects at every level. UiType is web/mobile-ios/mobile-android; GuidanceKind is foundation/pattern/style-recipe. domains is a nonempty unique subset of the following exact strings, sourced from PRD:85-94 [[c9]]: "Visual style", "Layout", "Color", "Typography", "Navigation and flows", "Components and states", "Motion and feedback", "Inclusive design", "Platform adaptation", "Content and trust". Color requires domainPayload.color, Layout requires domainPayload.layout, and Visual style requires domainPayload.style; multiple matching labels require all corresponding payloads. Other domain labels impose the common sc1 fields without inventing additional payload fields. IDs use namespace:slug (lowercase ASCII letters/digits with internal ._- separators), max 128 bytes; recordVersion/releaseId/digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex-64. Require nonblank problem, title, explanation, rationale, nonempty tradeoffs/suitableConditions, unique uiTypes; empty contraindications, units, relations and modificationNotes are allowed and meaningful. Original authorship needs author and may have no external sourceRefs; imported/derived/inferred entries require sourceRefs except independently inferred originals explicitly described in rationale and author attribution. Publication requires at least one example and one misuse for each declared UI type, each contentRef within inventory. Color domain requires nonempty unique semantic roles and pairings to declared roles; Layout requires content priority/adaptation rules; Visual style requires all style subfields. Checks require nonblank check and limits; requiredInputs/exceptions may be empty. Zero checks requires nonblank noMeasurableChecksRationale. Review is required even in drafts; publication rejects draft, empty reviewer/time/digest, invalid UTC ISO date, or contentDigest unequal to recordVersion. Authorship is never relabeled as imported/source-authored by review.

Implement sc2 in the same contracts module. schemaVersion is literal 1; no migrations or permissive unknown fields. Require at least one record and file, unique recordId and path, exact byte digest for each declared file and all referenced entries. Every record path appears in files and its bytes decode to the declared recordId/version. Exactly one sourceManifestPath, noticesPath and coveragePath reference listed files. Keep source and coverage file content opaque to s1 except for hashing; downstream stage assessments validate their semantics. Paths are package-relative POSIX names, case-sensitive but reject case-fold collisions for portability; reject empty, absolute, drive/UNC, backslash, NUL/control, dot and dot-dot segments, percent escapes and symlinks/non-regular inventory entries. Reject undeclared files. Relationship targets resolve to exact record pairs in this package, with no fallback; duplicate/self references and cycles among current record versions are invalid. Symmetric conceptual relations use one directed edge or an explicitly older included version only where unique record IDs permit it; no mutually self-referential current-version hashes. This v1 release therefore uses one directed edge for symmetric relations. Runtime availability overlays remain sc7/S004.

Implement exact sc1 shape, validating all three identifiers. It is an immutable value; no default release lookup, filesystem resolution or project identity is introduced. Pure JSON round-trip fixtures exercise ac2; actual daemon retrieval/lineage hydration remains S004. Return original sourceRefs, never replace them with source excerpts.

Implement exact sc2 code/path/message shape. Schema and semantic phases return deterministic issues sorted by JSON Pointer path then code and message. Stable categories: schema.unsupported, schema.invalid, guidance.incomplete, provenance.incomplete, domain.invalid, review.required, review.stale, reference.missing, reference.cycle, path.invalid, inventory.invalid, digest.mismatch, assessment.missing, assessment.failed, assessment.stale, limit.exceeded. Diagnostics carry no raw content or local absolute paths. Schema-first failures prevent unsafe deep traversal; valid siblings can still yield independent issues. Candidate size limits are explicit rejections, never truncation: record JSON <=1 MiB, package <=64 MiB, <=10,000 files, nesting depth <=64; these are format safety limits for v1, not search result limits.

Proposed src/design/corpus/canonical.ts defines pure canonical serialization and hashes. Accept only finite JSON values, plain data objects/arrays, valid Unicode scalar strings and safe finite numeric values; reject undefined/functions/symbols/BigInt/NaN/Infinity, accessors and non-plain objects at object entry points. Object keys sorted by JS UTF-16 code-unit lexicographic order; arrays preserve order except manifest records/files are explicitly sorted by ID/path for manifest digest. Serialize UTF-8 with no BOM/newline, JSON string escaping and JSON number representation, normalize -0 to 0, preserve other string contents without Unicode normalization. These rules are an insrc format, not a claim of RFC conformance. RecordVersion hashes canonical record excluding only top-level recordVersion and review; order changes in meaningful arrays therefore create a new version. review.contentDigest equals recordVersion. Candidate content digest hashes the canonical object {records:[{recordId,recordVersion}],files:[{path,digest}]} with record pairs sorted by ID/version and files sorted by path, excluding manifest and the coverage/review-envelope file. Coverage lives at coveragePath and is the sole v1 editorial envelope; reviewDigest hashes its canonical decoded JSON, including its supplied candidateContentDigest. All other listed files, including source manifest, notices and specimens, are included in candidate digest. Final releaseId/PublicationCheck.manifestDigest hash the canonical manifest with releaseId omitted, records/files sorted and reviewDigest included; manifest itself is not listed. No final releaseId may appear in coverage payload. Raw file hashes always cover exact file bytes, distinct from semantic canonical hashes. Test vectors pin every stage; content change invalidates review. No existing workflow epic hash helper is reused because its truncated run-ID semantics differ.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Own exact runtime/static record, evidence and provenance shapes plus pure content identity/round-trip invariants. New implementation paths are src/design/corpus/contracts.ts, canonical.ts and validate.ts; no existing API is modified.

Own manifest/issue/preflight envelopes and pure structural/domain/digest validation. Define a dependency-inverted assessment input for downstream eligibility and coverage validators; do not import or implement sc3/sc4. Missing assessments always block. Public barrel src/design/corpus/index.ts exports only these foundational schemas/types and validation/hash helpers; exact helper names are local implementation choices under the owned contracts, not existing code claims.

errorCases.scenario: Required field missing, invalid schema version or unknown property
errorCases.detection: Runtime closed schema validates unknown input before semantic traversal; literal schemaVersion check distinguishes unsupported version.
errorCases.response: Return schema.invalid or schema.unsupported with JSON Pointer; eligible false.
errorCases.userImpact: Curator sees exact field to correct; no publication.

errorCases.scenario: Unreviewed content or content changed since review
errorCases.detection: Compare reviewed status, reviewer/time and review.contentDigest against freshly computed recordVersion.
errorCases.response: review.required or review.stale; no trusted record projection.
errorCases.userImpact: Needs editorial review of the corrected content.

errorCases.scenario: Invalid domain payload, platform examples or source attribution
errorCases.detection: Conditional domain validators, declared-platform example/misuse matrix and authorship-specific provenance checks detect omissions.
errorCases.response: domain.invalid, guidance.incomplete or provenance.incomplete; keep authorship unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: Tampered, ambiguous or incomplete package inventory
errorCases.detection: Recompute raw byte hashes; compare manifest membership; validate unique IDs/paths, path grammar, references and relation DAG before final digest checks.
errorCases.userImpact: Candidate must be rebuilt; no repair or silent normalization.

errorCases.detection: Require exactly one eligibility and one coverage result, each bound to current candidateContentDigest; reject passed=true with nonempty issues.
errorCases.userImpact: No placeholder source/coverage approval is accepted.

errorCases.scenario: Input exceeds safety bounds or is not canonical JSON data
errorCases.detection: Bounded pre-walk checks byte lengths, file count, nesting, numeric/string validity, object descriptors and cycles before hashing.
errorCases.response: limit.exceeded or schema.invalid without hashing/truncating offending content.
errorCases.userImpact: Split oversized data or correct serialization; cannot silently lose guidance.

edgeCases.input: An original record with no upstream source
edgeCases.expected: Author, rationale, version and review remain required; empty sourceRefs is valid and no upstream provenance is fabricated.
Accept only with explicit noMeasurableChecksRationale; never imply automated accessibility certification.

edgeCases.input: One record applies to all three UI types
edgeCases.expected: Requires example and misuse for each; shared example bytes can be referenced more than once without duplicating inventory files.

edgeCases.input: Object key order or manifest inventory order differs
edgeCases.expected: Canonical identity remains stable; ordinary guidance-array order remains meaningful.

edgeCases.input: Valid draft with empty review details
edgeCases.expected: Draft schema accepts the complete shape; publication preflight rejects it until reviewed.
Empty arrays are explicit valid declarations, not absent metadata.

invariantsToPreserve.text: No schema coercion, default injection or stripping; preserve every validated lineage field.
Pure validation/hash routines never access DB, filesystem, network, LLMs or daemon runtime state.
Follow approved digest order and story ownership; no sc3/sc4/sc5/sc6/sc7 implementation in s1.

review-binding: draft exclusion and stale-content rejection

digest-chain: record→candidate→review→release no self reference, changed-content invalidation

Small complete in-memory package inventory with no real third-party assets

subjects: manifest-inventory: exact bytes/path/membership, digest tamper, duplicate/case collision, missing target and relation-cycle rejection
publication-composition: missing/duplicate/failed/stale assessments always block; valid fixed assessments pass

Stub downstream assessment results that exercise composition without implementing licensing/coverage engines

subjects: Import compiled corpus barrel in a fresh process with no daemon/DB/provider setup

alternativesConsidered.name: Schema-first typed contracts
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Define runtime schemas once and derive TypeScript shapes, with separate semantic validation.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Use the installed TypeBox and AJV dependencies for closed JSON schemas matching sc1/sc2. Derive public record types from those schemas and keep cross-record, digest and domain invariants in pure validators.

Canonical hashing is an independent versioned utility. Publication preflight composes foundational checks with explicitly supplied downstream eligibility/coverage evidence; this story does not implement those policies.
pros: Runtime and TypeScript fields share one definition.
Schema failures and semantic failures remain distinguishable.
cons: Schema definitions must stay within the installed AJV dialect.
Semantic rules still require explicitly maintained validators and tests.

alternativesConsidered.name: TypeScript interfaces plus handwritten guards
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep sc1/sc2 interfaces and manually validate all fields.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Write TypeScript interfaces matching the HLD and handwritten parsers for each payload. Pure digest helpers and downstream evidence composition are unchanged.

Guards produce the same stable issue format, but every field's compile-time and runtime requirements are maintained separately.
pros: No schema-library coupling in domain declarations.
Validation flow can directly express domain rules.
cons: Each new field needs both interface and guard changes, increasing drift risk.
Complete nested error paths and unknown-property checks require custom machinery.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Feasible but duplicate guards increase ongoing consistency burden.

citations.quotedText: Visual style; Layout; Color; Typography; Navigation and flows; Components and states; Motion and feedback; Inclusive design; Platform adaptation; Content and trust
